title: Davy Jones moves from snare drum to saxophone
summary: Jones left snare drum, took up a saxophone after a stay in Chicago; Bill Russell relays that Jones was credited with teaching local players chords.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: How long did Jones stay on snare drum?
Oh not very long. He didn't like it. He didn't like it at all. And then what did he go to?
Where did he go to? Well he picked up a metal phone. It got real good. And he came down here. And he went to Chicago. When he came back, he came back with a saxophone.
We forgot to put the date on here Bill.

Manuel Sayles was saying last night when we picked this up or night before that he thought David Jones got the credit for really introducing cards. Before that nobody ever paid any attention between one card and another here to know what they were. That he's one of the first ones around here at least that ever taught the fellas what chords to play on any instrument. That was really conscious of what one card from another.
